nodes.title: Learning's D7 (main, 2026-11-09), extends dc-r7-card-board-authored-gate to certification. certifyBoardRef now counts an authored ref's separate wholes (fraction-bars bars, wholes@1 wholes) as wholes, as the live gate does (board-sync gateCtxFor authoredRef → refWholes). The condition: her line names each bar's parts, as a count ("12 barabar tukdon mein se 5") or a denominator ("3/5"). A bar her line never names still binds W8. Before this, certification counted the 2 outlines as an unspoken "2" ("rect x2") whenever her line did not say exactly two fractions. That covered the unshaded ribbons pose (no fraction said) and the 3/5 vs 4/10 reveal (three said: 3/5, 6/10, 4/10). Three c5-t02 cards had gone back to a line because of it: s3 checks[1], s2 rem1.then, s2 rem2.then. The live take already passed all of them. Reverse if a certified two-bar board is refused live, or a judge counts a bar the line did not name.

Learning's D7 (main, 2026-11-09): equal-groups@1 with `sizes` takes an optional `equalTo` {groups 2-6, each 1-8}, and groups × each must equal the sizes' sum (else groups_equal_to). Layout: the given groups take the left half, shared out from the heap as before, each with its count under it. A thin line separates them from the equal share on the right, which is drawn still: its own groups, each count under it. The share's dots are in the "good" ink and a shade smaller (r 4 against 4.5). Two reasons: they are what each WOULD get, and W8 counts them as their own family (16 beside 16, never "32"). Facts get equalShare ("4 groups of 4"); counts get equalTo {groups, each} (shared/whiteboard cleanCounts). c4's marble (7, 3, 3, 3 | 4 × 4) and pencil (6, 3, 3 | 3 × 4) answerBoards certify under their whys and verdicts. Under the pencil card's prompt the share's 4 fails W4: an answerBoard is drawn on the reveal, never under the prompt. Reverse if judges find the side-by-side share gives the answer away on a board shown before the reveal.
